draft.title: Map conventions
card: A useful map has five parts, often remembered as BOLTS: border, orientation, legend, title and scale.
orientation is a north arrow, which shows which way is north. The border is a frame around the map.
the legend explains what the colours and symbols mean. The scale links distance on the map to distance on the ground.
the title says what the map shows.
draft.remember: Check for all five BOLTS parts, as each one does a different job.

a.q: Sam wants to find the real distance between two towns shown on a map. Which map part should Sam use?
a.why: The scale links distance on the map to distance on the ground, so it gives real distances. The legend is tempting because it helps a reader use the map, but it only explains symbols and colours.
a.clue: Which part links map distance to ground distance?

b.q: Priya draws a map of bus stops in her town. A classmate cannot tell what the blue square symbols mean. Which part of her map should explain them?
b.why: The legend explains what the colours and symbols mean, so it tells the classmate what the blue squares show. The title is tempting because it describes the map, but it only says what the whole map shows, not what each symbol means.
b.clue: Which part explains the colours and symbols?
